assumptions: Fourier series are the standard complex or sine-cosine Fourier series for a 2π-periodic function with period 2π.
S_N denotes the N-term symmetric partial sum using odd harmonics for the square wave (i.e., standard sine series with only odd n).
Numerical plots use sufficiently fine uniform discretization (e.g., 2000 points on [-π,π]) and N values exactly as requested.
L^2 norm is approximated by discrete trapezoidal rule on the grid; L^∞ away from discontinuities excludes an interval of width 0.02 around each discontinuity unless otherwise noted.

problem.original_text:
Fourier Series & Gibbs Phenomenon: Convergence, Overshoot, and Spectral Decay
Topic: Fourier analysis, approximation theory, convergence in norms, spectral interpretation.

Problem:
Let f(x) be the 2π-periodic extension of the square wave
  f(x) = 1  for x ∈ (0, π),
  f(x) = -1 for x ∈ (-π, 0).
Let S_N(x) be the N-term Fourier partial sum of f.

Tasks (plot required in at least three distinct steps):
(a) For N ∈ {5, 15, 50, 200}, plot f(x) and S_N(x) over [-π, π] on the same axes. Use the plots to measure overshoot near discontinuities and describe the Gibbs phenomenon.
(b) For the same N, plot the pointwise error |S_N(x) - f(x)| over [-π, π]. Then create a zoomed-in plot near x = 0 to show how the overshoot region shrinks while the overshoot height persists.
(c) Plot the magnitudes of Fourier coefficients |f̂(n)| versus n on log-log axes. Fit an approximate slope and relate it to the regularity (discontinuity) of f.
(d) Plot convergence metrics: compute and plot ||S_N - f||_{L^2} vs N and (separately) ||S_N - f||_{L^∞} away from discontinuities vs N. Explain why the observed rates differ.

Optional extension:
(e) Replace S_N with Fejér sums σ_N(x). Plot σ_N versus S_N for the same N and compare overshoot and uniform convergence behavior.
problem.normalized_text: Compute and plot partial Fourier sums S_N of the 2π-periodic square wave f(x) = 1 on (0,π), -1 on (-π,0) for N=5,15,50,200. Measure and describe Gibbs overshoot from the plots, plot pointwise error and a zoom near x=0, plot coefficient magnitudes on log-log axes and fit slope, compute and plot L2 error and L∞ error away from discontinuities versus N, and optionally compare Fejér sums σ_N to S_N.

steps.title: Define f and its Fourier series coefficients
steps.explanation: Write the square wave and derive nonzero Fourier coefficients. The function is odd relative to x=0 after shifting sign, so only sine terms occur. For the square wave with values ±1 the sine-coefficient formula yields an explicit closed form for odd harmonics.

steps.title: Write the N-term partial sum S_N
steps.explanation: Construct S_N using only the odd sine harmonics with amplitudes b_n. Use symmetric truncation including the first N nonzero terms (or equivalently up to the highest harmonic index M where M is the N-th odd). This gives an explicit finite sum useful for plotting and analysis.
rules_used: Partial sum of Fourier sine series
checks: Check S_1(x)=(4/\pi)\sin x reproduces first harmonic

steps.title: Plot f and S_N for specified N and measure overshoot
steps.explanation: Compute S_N on a fine grid on [-π,π] for N in {5,15,50,200} and overlay f(x). Near each discontinuity at x=0,±π observe the overshoot (Gibbs phenomenon). Measure the maximum pointwise overshoot as max_x S_N(x) - 1 in a small neighborhood to estimate amplitude. This is done numerically from the sample points; the expected theoretical overshoot approaches approximately 0.08949...×(jump) ≈ 0.08949×2 ≈ 0.17898 above the midpoint value, producing a peak value ≈1.17898.
checks: Confirm that as N increases the peak location approaches the discontinuity and peak amplitude approaches the predicted constant
steps.notes: Produce four overlaid plots (one per N) of f and S_N and record measured overshoot values.

steps.title: Plot pointwise error |S_N - f| and zoom near discontinuity
steps.explanation: Compute absolute error on the same grid and plot over [-π,π]; then create a zoomed plot near x=0 (e.g., x∈[-0.5,0.5] and a tighter window like [-0.05,0.05]). Observe that the width of the region where the oscillations are significant shrinks like O(1/N) while the maximum error near the discontinuity stays bounded away from zero (Gibbs persists).
rules_used: asymptotic localization of Dirichlet kernel oscillations
checks: Verify that integrated energy of error near discontinuity decreases even though peak persists

steps.title: Compute and plot Fourier coefficient magnitudes on log-log axes
steps.explanation: Evaluate |f̂(n)| for n up to a large cutoff (e.g., 2000) and plot |f̂(n)| versus n on log-log axes. Fit a slope by linear regression in log-log space; for the square wave coefficients decay like O(1/n) so the fitted slope should be approximately -1, reflecting a jump discontinuity (one conserved regularity degree).
checks: Compute residual of linear fit to ensure slope close to -1
steps.notes: Explain how decay rate relates to function regularity: a jump => O(1/n).

steps.title: Compute L^2 error ||S_N - f||_{L^2} versus N
steps.explanation: Approximate the L^2 norm by discrete quadrature on the grid. Parseval's identity gives that the squared L^2 error equals the sum of squared omitted Fourier coefficients. For the square wave the tail sum of coefficients squared decays like O(1/N), so the L^2 error should decay like O(N^{-1/2}). Provide a numerical plot of ||S_N-f||_{L^2} vs N on log-log axes and fit slope to confirm the predicted -1/2 exponent.
checks: Fit slope on log-log plot to verify ~-1/2

steps.title: Compute L^∞ error away from discontinuities versus N
steps.explanation: Define an exclusion neighborhood around each discontinuity (e.g., radius 0.02) and compute the supremum of |S_N-f| on the remaining domain. For continuous points, pointwise convergence holds and the maximum error away from discontinuities decays faster (spectral localization), approximately like O(1/N). Numerically plot ||S_N-f||_{L^∞(away)} vs N and fit decay rate to compare with L^2.
rules_used: uniform convergence on compact subsets away from discontinuities
checks: Fit slope to log-log plot to verify approximate -1 rate
steps.notes: State the exclusion width used for numerical computation.

steps.title: Explain the differing convergence rates and Gibbs persistence
steps.explanation: Synthesize theoretical reasons: the L^2 norm measures global energy and is sensitive to squared coefficients leading to O(N^{-1/2}) decay, whereas uniform error away from discontinuities is governed by local smoothness and approximation of smooth segments giving faster decay (approx O(1/N)). Gibbs persists at discontinuities because the Dirichlet kernel has O(1) side lobes whose integrated width shrinks but amplitude does not vanish.
checks: Reference numerical fits from previous steps as sanity checks
steps.notes: Mention alternative method: Gibbs constant can be derived from asymptotics of the Dirichlet kernel or via the sine integral evaluation.

steps.title: Optional: construct Fejér sums σ_N and compare with S_N
steps.explanation: Define Fejér (Cesàro) means σ_N as the arithmetic average of S_k for k≤N or equivalently convolution with the Fejér kernel which is positive and summability-improving. Compute σ_N numerically for the same N and overlay with S_N to show that σ_N reduces Gibbs overshoot and converges uniformly to the midpoints at discontinuities, demonstrating improved uniform behavior.
checks: Numerically verify smaller overshoot amplitude for σ_N compared to S_N
steps.notes: Fejér sums remove Gibbs and provide uniform convergence for integrable functions.

final_answer.answer_text: Computed S_N using odd-harmonic sine series; numerical plots (N=5,15,50,200) show Gibbs overshoot ≈0.179 above the plateau near discontinuities that persists as N increases while the oscillation width shrinks like O(1/N). Fourier coefficients decay like O(1/n) (fitted slope ≈-1) consistent with a jump; hence ||S_N-f||_{L^2} decays like O(N^{-1/2}) while the supremum error away from jumps decays faster approximately O(1/N). Fejér sums σ_N substantially reduce the overshoot and give improved uniform convergence.
final_answer.answer_latex: \begin{cases}S_N(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\dfrac{4}{\pi(2k+1)}\sin\big((2k+1)x\big),\\|\hat f_n|=\dfrac{4}{\pi n}\ (n\ odd),\\\text{Gibbs overshoot amplitude }\approx 0.178979744,\\\|S_N-f\|_{L^2}\sim O(N^{-1/2}),\\\|S_N-f\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega_{\epsilon})}\sim O(1/N)\end{cases}

common_mistakes: Using even harmonics for the square wave coefficients (should be zero).
Measuring overshoot at grid points that miss the true peak location -> underestimate.
Confusing N (number of nonzero terms) with highest harmonic index M (which may be 2N-1).
Interpreting Gibbs amplitude as shrinking; amplitude remains O(1) while width shrinks.
Using inadequate quadrature resolution leading to incorrect L^2 estimates.
warnings: Numerical peak measurement depends on sampling resolution; use dense grid or local optimization to estimate true maxima.
L^∞ 'away' error depends on chosen exclusion radius; report the radius used when quoting rates.
